faqs.question: Can I remove the ink cartridges from the product if I'm not using the product?
faqs.answer:
No. The ink cartridges should remain installed in the product even when the product is not being used.
Note:
The ink delivery system is not sealed when the ink cartridges are removed. This may allow debris to enter the ink delivery system, which may cause damage.

faqs.question: What is the composition of the ink in the ink cartridges?
faqs.answer:
The ink for your product is water-based and nontoxic. For more information, see
Safety Data Sheets
page.

faqs.question: How long can I use the ink cartridges after they are installed?
faqs.answer: For best printing results, expend the ink cartridges within 6 months of installation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Epson Device Admin software and the Epson Web Config utility?
faqs.answer:
Both applications manage Epson printers that are connected to a network. However, the Epson Device Admin software will allow you to configure and monitor multiple Epson printers at one time. The Epson Web Config utility will allow you to configure and monitor one Epson printer at a time. See below for a list of supported features.
Epson Device Admin and Epson Web Config
Note:
The features listed below are supported remotely over a network.
Configure a single printer.
Display a printer's ink supply level and usage counter.
Import and export printer configuration settings to back up or clone configuration settings to another printer.
Check and update the firmware version of a single printer.
Epson Device Admin
Epson Device Admin supports these features, in addition to those listed above.
Send an email alert when an error occurs on the printer.*
Schedule and send an email that reports the printer's usage.*
Schedule and implement a firmware update.
Configure multiple Epson printers via a template.
* Email services need to be configured in the Epson Device Admin software to use these features.
Note:
Other Epson scanners, inkjet printers, and large format printers may include an option to send an email alert from the Epson Web Config utility. For support with these products, consult the product's user manual.

faqs.question: How do I replace the maintenance box?
faqs.answer:
Make sure you have a new maintenance box before you begin.
Note:
When you see a message on the LCD screen indicating the maintenance box is at the end of its service life, it should be replaced promptly.
CAUTION:
Do not reuse a maintenance box that has been removed and left uninstalled for more than a week. Keep the maintenance box away from direct sunlight.
Remove the new maintenance box from its package.
Open the paper cover and then open the maintenance box cover.
Grasp the maintenance box and pull it out of its holder.
Place the used maintenance box in the bag that came with the new maintenance box.
Insert the new maintenance box into the holder and push it in all the way.
Close the maintenance box cover.
Dispose of the used maintenance box at your local recycling center.

faqs.question: The quality of the print on my labels does not appear as I expected. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Make sure you print on compatible media. See the product's technical reference guide for information.
Print a nozzle check pattern to see if any of the nozzles are clogged. Clean the print head, if necessary.
Make sure the paper type setting in the software matches the type of media you loaded in the product.
Make sure you load the printable side of the paper correctly in the product.
Adjust the print quality settings in the product's software.

faqs.question: Should the ink cartridges remain installed when I transport my product?
faqs.answer: Yes. Leave the ink cartridges installed. Removing the cartridges can dry out the print head and may prevent the product from printing.

faqs.question: How do I replace the ink cartridges?
faqs.answer:
Make sure you have your replacement ink cartridges handy before you begin. You must install new ink cartridges immediately after removing the old ones. Do the following:
Open the left ink cartridge cover.
Note:
The illustrations show the CW-C6500A model, but the instructions apply to all models unless otherwise specified.
Press the lever down to remove the expended ink cartridge.
Remove the new ink cartridge from the packaging and shake it side to side.
Slide the ink cartridge into the slot for the cartridge until it clicks.
Repeat steps 2 to 4 for each ink cartridge you want to install.
Close the cover.

faqs.question: Which black ink type (gloss or matte) is recommended for my label application?
faqs.answer: Matte ink is the best choice if all printing will be done on matte media. If you will be printing on any gloss media, we recommend gloss black ink. If you are uncertain of which type of media you want to use, we recommend you select gloss black ink. Both ink types have BS5609 certification.

faqs.question: How do I set up a new printer to use gloss or matte black ink?
faqs.answer: Select the type of ink you want to use during the printer's initial setup. The printer will prompt you to select the type of ink you are installing on the printer's front panel. See the image below for the steps.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the gloss and matte black inks?
faqs.answer:
The gloss and matte black ink are highly durable pigment-based inks and are BS5609 certified
1
. The matte black ink creates a darker black when printed on matte media and a richer image on plain media. The gloss black ink is similar to the ink used by the Epson ColorWorks C7500G. The gloss black ink can be used to print on a wider range of substrates.
Note:
1
Requires BS5609-certified label material for use with the printer and the ink system.

faqs.question: How should I clean the peeler for my product?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Turn off the product and unplug the power cable.
Disconnect any other cables connected to the product.
Open the peeler cover and remove all the paper loaded in the product.
Note:
Do not use compressed air to clean the product.
Clean the rollers with a cotton swab moistened with alcohol.
Daily cleaning is recommended to maintain good print quality.
For more information, see the Cleaning the Peeler video on
YouTube
.

faqs.question: Paper jammed in my product. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Open the front cover and remove any paper.
Open the paper cover and remove the spindle, if necessary.
Raise the release lever.
Remove any jammed paper and then lower the release lever.
Close the paper cover and front cover.
Select
Pause
from the product's control panel. The paper jam should be cleared.
For more information, see the Paper is jammed section in the printer's
User's Guide
.

faqs.question: I can't get odd shaped media to feed into the printer. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The gap sensors may need to be adjusted to detect the media. Do the following:
Turn off the printer, if necessary.
Make sure there is no media in the printer. If necessary, press the
Back Feed
button on the printer's control panel.
Open the paper cover.
Locate the gap sensors (the two gray bars near the media feed slot).
Important:
The sensors must be positioned at the highest point of the odd shaped media.
Make sure the receiver sensor (top) and the emitter sensor (bottom) line up with each.
Note:
Use a small screwdriver to line up the sensors.
Try feeding the media again.

faqs.question: Which type of media can I print on?
faqs.answer:
Coated media for inkjet printers works best, but you can also use uncoated media. If                 you use uncoated media, you should test the media for image quality and to confirm                 if it meets your performance requirements.
For a list of compatible media for Epson ColorWorks printers, see the Compatible                 Media List on our
Color Label                     Printers
page. Epson works with all major media manufacturers to identify compatible inkjet media                 for Epson ColorWorks printers. There is a wide variety of media, which includes clear, semi-gloss and                 BS5609-certified media.
Epson label media is available in Premium Matte, High Gloss, and Durable Matte                 Synthetic media types for the ColorWorks C3500, C6000 Series, and C7500 Series                 printers. This media is available in standard sizes.For more information, see our
Color Label Printers
page. You can order the media from Epson ProFocus ColorWorks and NSP channels.
Note:
Do not use pinfed media.

faqs.question: I can't save my printer driver settings on my Mac. Is there anything I can do?
faqs.answer: No, the Mac operating system resets all settings when a print window is opened. This is a restriction of the operating system.

faqs.question: Can I add a cutter or a peeler to the product?
